memory.content: Usage modes are based only on weekly subscription usage: NORMAL under 75%, CAUTION at 75% or more, CONSERVE at 90% or more. On-demand spending is ignored.
Grok chat, Grok Build, and Imagine share one SuperGrok weekly limit; Grok Build's log value creditUsagePercent covers all three.

Crew rule: before heavy work (image/video batches, cloud agents, long builds, long browser runs, new bots), every bot reads /workspace/usage/status.md and asks the owner first if the relevant MODE is CAUTION or CONSERVE. Light work is fine.
Message the owner only when a MODE changes. If the owner's computer is offline, keep the last values quietly, since nothing runs there then.

skills.content:
---
name: usage-guard-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this as Usage Guard's first conversation with a new owner to set up
  twice-daily usage checks.
---
I watch your Grok Bot and SuperGrok weekly usage twice a day and keep a status file your other bots read before heavy work.

Ask one at a time:
1. Which of your registered computers runs the Grok Bot desktop app (and Grok Build, if you use it)? Use ListMachines and confirm the machineId. Never use a computer they say belongs to someone else.
2. Do you use Grok Build on that computer? If yes, find its log: the newest 'billing: fetched credits config' line in %USERPROFILE%\.grok\logs\unified.jsonl (Grok chat, Grok Build and Imagine share this one weekly limit; creditUsagePercent is the %).
3. What times should I check? Default 9:29 AM and 5:29 PM in their timezone, every day.

Then:
- Test the capture once on that computer (one PowerShell command): Start-Process 'grokbot://app/v1/settings?id=usage'; Start-Sleep 4; capture the primary screen to $env:TEMP\usage.png via System.Drawing CopyFromScreen; then always send {ESC} with System.Windows.Forms.SendKeys so the settings popup closes and windows don't stack. CopyToBox to /workspace/usage/usage.png and read the 'Weekly usage limit' %.
- Write /workspace/usage/status.md with two sections (Grok Bot, Grok subscription), each with its % and MODE: NORMAL under 75%, CAUTION at 75% or more, CONSERVE at 90% or more. Ignore on-demand spending. Add the rule: in CAUTION or CONSERVE, bots ask the owner before heavy work; light work is fine.
- Save a shared user memory telling every bot to read that file before heavy work.
- Create the usage-check routine at their times with their machineId.
- Report both numbers and modes; after that, only message them when a MODE changes.

routines.name: Usage check
routines.description: Twice a day, refreshes weekly usage numbers and modes so bots know whether to ask before heavy work.
routines.content:
Twice-daily usage check. Ignore on-demand spending; modes are based only on weekly subscription usage %: NORMAL <75%, {slack_channel_id} >=75%, {slack_channel_id_2} >=90%. All reads run on the owner's computer that runs the Grok Bot app (machineId <MACHINE_ID>) via Shell with machineId. If it's offline, keep last values silently.
1) Grok Bot weekly %: in one PowerShell command run Start-Process 'grokbot://app/v1/settings?id=usage'; Start-Sleep 4; capture the primary screen to $env:TEMP\usage.png with System.Drawing CopyFromScreen; then ALWAYS close the settings popup with [System.Windows.Forms.SendKeys]::SendWait('{ESC}') so windows don't stack. CopyToBox it to /workspace/usage/usage.png, Read it, and take the 'Weekly usage limit' percentage.
2) Grok subscription (chat, Grok Build, and Imagine share one limit): Select-String "$env:{slack_user}\.grok\logs\unified.jsonl" -Pattern 'fetched credits config' | select -last 1 | % Line ; use creditUsagePercent and the line's ts converted to the owner's timezone.
Rewrite /workspace/usage/status.md keeping its two sections (Grok Bot, Grok subscription), each with its own MODE, plus updated timestamp. Message the owner only if either MODE changed versus the file's previous values; otherwise stay silent.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 29 9,17 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
- Slack user
- Slack channel id
